Excellence, Honesty, KindnessWelcome to Orchard House School
Welcome to Orchard House School, a leading co-educational private school in Chiswick, West London, welcoming children aged 3 to 11 from Nursery through to Year 6. As part of the Dukes Education family, we combine the warmth of a close-knit community with the ambition and resources of a wider network of leading UK schools.
At Orchard House, Excellence is nurtured, Honesty is encouraged, and Kindness is second nature. We balance ambition with attentiveness, helping every child flourish academically and personally, in a school that families across West London and beyond choose for its blend of rigour and genuine care.
“Pupils love the happiness at this close-knit Chiswick prep”
TATLER SCHOOLS GUIDE
MEET OURHead
I hold a deep belief that children are at their best when they feel safe, happy and are inspired to try their very best every day.
DiscoverOur Exceptional 11+ Results
We are delighted to share our 2026 11+ results.
Our Year 6 cohort received 150 offers and 42 scholarships to 27 leading day and boarding schools across the UK. These included awards across Art, Drama, Music, Sport and Academics – reflecting the breadth of talent developed during their time at Orchard House.
At Orchard House, we pride ourselves on preparing children not just for exams, but for the next stage of their education and beyond. Through a broad and ambitious curriculum, The Learning Orchard, alongside outstanding pastoral care, pupils are supported to discover their strengths, develop confidence and grow into well-rounded individuals. These outcomes reflect that ethos. Alongside academic success, we place equal importance on character – nurturing pupils who are kind, curious and confident in themselves.
Read more about the 11+ at Orchard House.
Orchard House helps children grow and thrive in so many ways. As well as academia, there are excellent opportunities with sports and the arts.
EXPLORE OURCurriculum
Our innovative curriculum, The Learning Orchard, includes dedicated time in our state-of-the-art Innovation Hub for hands-on learning, a Philosophy and Oracy programme that encourages confident communication, and the Reading Scholar or Reading Explorer programmes, for KS2 and KS1 respectively, which foster a love of reading and support independent literacy development.
Ages 3-5Early Years
Give your child the best start in a nurturing, joyful and inspiring environment. Our Early Years team sparks curiosity, builds confidence and supports every child as they explore, play and learn in bright classrooms and engaging outdoor spaces. Discover a place where young learners feel happy, valued and ready to thrive.
Ages 5-7Pre-Prep
In Pre-Prep, your child will grow in confidence, independence and curiosity. We’ll nurture their love of learning through inspiring lessons, rich stories, hands-on exploration and specialist teaching. With plenty of room for creativity and discovery, we’ll help your child build strong foundations while ensuring they feel happy, supported and excited for each new day.
Ages 7-11Prep
In our Prep-School, we’ll challenge and support your child as they move into a more ambitious, academically focused stage of their learning. Through our bespoke Learning Orchard curriculum — with its rich blend of Powerful Knowledge, Holistic Learning, Leadership and World Readiness — your child will be inspired to think deeply, question confidently and develop a genuine love of learning. With expert teaching in English, Maths, Science and Reasoning, they’ll gain the skills, curiosity and resilience needed to excel in the real world.
PATHWAY TO SENIOR SCHOOLSenior Schools & 11+
By Year 6, your child will be exceptionally well prepared for entry to a senior school that matches their abilities, character and interests. Recognising that the 11+ is just one element of this journey, we deliver a comprehensive programme of senior school preparation that combines expert exam coaching with thoughtful, high-quality interview preparation. As a Dukes Education prep, Orchard House pupils also receive priority entry into Dukes senior schools.

Shaping the Future, Today.
At Orchard House School, our ethos underpins everything we do. We believe that children thrive when they are happy, supported, and inspired to achieve their best. Our aim is to provide an education that not only prepares pupils for senior school but equips them with the skills, values and confidence to flourish in life.
Our Ethos in Action
The ethos of Orchard House is lived out in every classroom, playground and corridor. Each day, our community works together by:
Putting children at the centre of everything we do with a forward-looking approach to education
Valuing each child as an individual, nurturing their talents and celebrating their uniqueness
Treating all members of our community with respect, courtesy, kindness and concern
Creating a welcoming, supportive environment that fosters teamwork and belonging
Recognising and celebrating achievement in every sphere: academic, creative, sporting and personal
Building resilience and perseverance so children are ready for life’s challenges and opportunities
A warm and friendly school with strong academic underpinnings and excellent support for all, producing confident, articulate, self-aware and happy children.
Our Values
Excellence
We offer a broad, balanced curriculum, expert teaching, and exceptional enrichment opportunities so that every child can discover their passions and excel. From science and humanities to sport, music, art and drama, pupils are encouraged to aim high and embrace challenge. We prepare them for extraordinary futures.
Honesty
We believe in genuine, respectful relationships built on trust. Pupils learn the courage to be themselves, to take responsibility, and to see mistakes as part of the learning journey. Honesty builds resilience and strength of character, preparing our children for life beyond Orchard House.
Kindness
Kindness is the foundation of true leadership. We encourage pupils to show compassion to others and themselves, learning that kindness requires courage, empathy and respect. By leading with kindness, our children develop the ability to uplift those around them and create positive change in the world.
Our values run through every aspect of Orchard House life. They shape the way we learn, play and grow together.
Every Child Learns Differently
We know that no two children learn in the same way. Our teaching draws on a variety of methods from Montessori-inspired approaches in the Early Years to kinaesthetic, oral, tactile and visual learning throughout the school. Small class sizes mean we can tailor learning to each child, helping them build confidence and resilience.
At Orchard House, mistakes are never failures, they are signs of effort and growth. We encourage every child to try, persevere, and support one another. As a co-educational school, boys and girls learn alongside one another, preparing them for the real world where collaboration, respect and teamwork matter most.
Looking Ahead
As the world continues to evolve, so too must we. Orchard House is proud to remain at the forefront of education, combining tradition with innovation to prepare pupils for the future.
Our Development Plan outlines our ambitious vision for the coming years, ensuring we continue to provide an exceptional and forward-thinking learning experience for every child.

Mrs Henrietta AdamsWelcome from our Head
It is a privilege to lead Orchard House School, a thriving and joyful community in the heart of West London. As one of the area’s leading prep schools, we are proud of our reputation not only for outstanding academic results, but also for nurturing the unique talents of every child.
At Orchard House, children are at the centre of everything we do. Small classes, dedicated teachers and an award-winning approach to pastoral care ensure that every pupil feels safe, happy and valued. We know that children learn best when they feel safe and engaged, and our aim is always to provide an environment where they can flourish.
We are proud to be a co-educational school, welcoming boys and girls from the ages of 3 to 11. Our bespoke curriculum, The Learning Orchard, combined with our expert approach to the 11+ , equips pupils to move on to leading senior schools in London and beyond. Each year, many of our children achieve scholarships in academics, sport, music, drama, art and chess. Yet what matters most is that every pupil finds the school that is right for them, where they will continue to thrive.
As we prepare our pupils for an ever-changing world, we focus not only on outstanding teaching and learning but also on our values that underpin true success: Excellence, Honesty and Kindness. We want our children to develop a love of learning, an appreciation of hard work, and a sense of responsibility for others. Alongside this, our rich programme of enrichment opportunities helps them discover new skills and passions that will support them throughout their lives.
Above all, Orchard House is a community. Pupils, parents and staff come together to create a warm and caring environment where achievement and enjoyment go hand in hand. There is plenty of laughter alongside the hard work, and a genuine spirit of support that extends well beyond the classroom.
This is an exciting moment in Orchard House’s story, and I warmly invite you to visit us to experience the energy, warmth and ambition of our school for yourself.
Meet our Head Mrs Henrietta Adams
Henrietta Adams has lived in West London for most of her life, having grown up in Bedford Park, Chiswick. She studied French and Music at the University of London before qualifying as a solicitor, but her passion for education soon led her to retrain as a teacher at the Institute of Education.
Henrietta began her teaching career at Chiswick & Bedford Park Preparatory School (CBPPS) in 2011, where she went on to become Director of Studies, Assistant Head, and later Headmistress in 2020. Following the merger of CBPPS with Orchard House, she was appointed Head of Orchard House School in 2024.
Fluent in French and a talented musician, Henrietta plays both the flute and piano. Outside of school she enjoys skiing and sailing, hobbies she shares with her family.
Favourite thing about OHS: “The laughter you hear every day around the school. It’s such a joyful place to be.”
Favourite subject as a child: “French. I had the most amazing teacher who made me fall in love with the language and the country!”
Pupils would be surprised to know: “I studied Music alongside French at university and love playing my flute and piano.”
At Orchard House, our goal is simple: for every child to feel happy, valued and inspired to achieve their very best. We want our pupils to leave us not only with excellent academic foundations, but with confidence, kindness and a genuine love of learning that will stay with them for life.”

Our Performing Arts Ethos
Music and Drama at Orchard House aren’t just subjects; they are vibrant, joyful cornerstones of school life that spark creativity, build confidence and create unforgettable memories for our children. From their earliest days in Eurhythmics, where rhythm, movement and music come alive through play, our pupils are encouraged to listen, imagine and create. As they progress, they are supported to explore their individual talents, whether that’s composing, acting, singing, playing an instrument, working behind the scenes or a combination of them all. Our inclusive approach ensures every child has the opportunity to shine.
The strength of our Music and Drama provision is reflected in our children’s success. In the past year alone, 14 scholarships have been awarded to leading senior schools across both disciplines. Pupils also achieve recognition at regional music and drama festivals, receiving awards and commendations for their talent and commitment.
“The OHS music team shows up with passion and deep dedication to both the children and the music.”
Music
Music at Orchard House is thriving. Each week, over 200 individual lessons take place across a wide range of instruments, from piano and violin to guitar, drums and voice. Specialist peripatetic teachers guide and inspire pupils at every level – whether they are discovering their first notes or preparing for advanced performance opportunities.
Music Curriculum
In the classroom, music is introduced from the earliest years. Our Nursery children are introduced to eurhythmics, a movement-based approach that uses play to develop rhythm, coordination and listening. As they progress, pupils explore percussion, recorders, ukuleles, music technology and composition. Singing and music appreciation are at the heart of lessons, exposing pupils to diverse genres and encouraging both enjoyment and analysis.
A distinctive highlight is our Wider Opportunities scheme in Year 3. Every pupil is given the chance to try woodwind, string, and brass instruments, with free instrument loans and weekly tuition. This opens the door to ensemble playing and sparks new musical passions. To support formal progression, Orchard House also hosts in-house ABRSM exam sessions each term. This provides pupils with a supportive environment to showcase their progress and celebrate achievement.
Productions & Performances
The energy of our music culture extends far beyond lessons. Pupils can join over 12 ensembles, from flute and recorder groups to strings, brass, guitars and an A Cappella choir. Our school orchestra continues to grow in size and ambition, while five choirs thrive across the school – from Juniors and Seniors to Chamber Choir and even a Parent & Teacher Choir.
Performance is at the heart of this culture. Pupils take to the stage in concerts, Rising Stars recitals, and weekly assemblies, as well as major events such as the Carol Concert, Spring Concert and the much-loved Petter Cup Musician of the Year competition. Watch Phoebe’s 2025 winning performance below. Many also represent the school in external competitions, including the Richmond and Ealing Music Festivals, and perform at community events such as the Bedford Park Festival. These experiences build confidence, celebrate talent and nurture a lifelong love of performing.
Drama
Drama at Orchard House provides pupils with the chance to step into new roles, stories, and creative experiences. It develops confidence, creativity, and collaboration, while giving every child a voice on stage.
Drama Curriculum
From the Early Years onwards, drama is woven into the school week. For our youngest pupils, lessons focus on imaginative play, storytelling and developing early performance skills. As children progress, they explore techniques such as improvisation, freeze-frame, devised theatre and character development. Pupils are also introduced to backstage skills, including lighting, sound and even camera work to broaden their understanding of how theatre comes to life.
Productions & Performances
Performance is at the heart of our drama journey. Nursery and Reception children begin with magical Nativity plays, while Years 1 and 2 enjoy festive productions that give them their first chance to perform with microphones on stage. Each year, pupils grow in confidence through class assemblies and drama festivals, before culminating in the Year 6 Summer Production at the POSK Theatre. Complete with live music, lighting, and staging, recent shows such as Shrek! The Musical Jr and Oliver! have been truly spectacular highlights for pupils and parents alike.

Orchard House Is Proudly Working Towards High Performance Learning (HPL) World Class School Accreditation
At Orchard House, we believe every child can thrive with the right support, challenge and opportunities. High Performance Learning (HPL) strengthens this belief and sits naturally alongside The Learning Orchard — our bespoke curriculum designed to nurture curious, confident and capable young people.
As we work towards HPL World Class School Accreditation, we continue to deepen our commitment to exceptional teaching and learning, ensuring every child is encouraged to aim high and grow in confidence.
What is HPL?
High Performance Learning is a research-based approach developed by Professor Deborah Eyre. It is built on the belief that high achievement is not fixed or reserved for a select few. With the right teaching, mindset and opportunities, every child can develop the skills and behaviours needed to succeed.
At Orchard House, we talk about performance rather than ability. In our classrooms, “I can’t do this” becomes “I can’t do this yet”. This language helps children build resilience, embrace challenge and develop a lifelong love of learning.
HPL at Orchard House
High Performance Learning provides a shared language for learning across the school. It helps children understand not only what they are learning, but how they learn best. At the heart of HPL are two key elements:
1. Values, Attitudes and Attributes (VAAs):
These focus on how children approach learning, for example resilience, empathy, hard work and open-mindedness
2. Advanced Cognitive Performance Characteristics (ACPs):
These focus on how children think, for example analysing, linking ideas and reflecting on their thinking.
These elements are not taught as separate lessons. They are woven throughout everyday teaching, classroom discussion and learning experiences across the school. Over time, children begin to recognise these behaviours in themselves and others, helping them become more reflective, independent and ambitious learners.
HPL complements the vision behind The Learning Orchard Curriculum: an ambitious, knowledge-rich curriculum designed to prepare children for a changing world.
Together, they help us nurture pupils who are knowledgeable, inquisitive, adaptable and quietly confident — children who are ready not only to succeed academically, but to thrive beyond the classroom.

We actively encourage a close relationship between parents and all staff. Sharing information gives us a deeper insight into the wellbeing and progress of each child, and our open-door policy means we’re readily available to discuss any concerns that arise.
Parents are encouraged to support their child’s learning, and the school gives guidance on how best this can be achieved. Parents are also invited to regular parents’ evenings, open mornings, sports days, concerts, class assemblies, and theatrical productions. They can also join in their child’s class to share special events or celebrate a religious festival.
At the end of each autumn term parents are invited to the school Christmas plays or concerts. In the spring or summer term the children in Form 2 and the Upper School invite their parents to see their play. The children in the Den and Lower 1 invite their parents to an assembly.
Throughout the year there are opportunities for parents to watch various sporting events. All fixtures and team lists can be viewed on the sports section of the school website. Parents of children in Forms 3 and above are invited to the Orchard House swimming galas and gymnastics displays. All parents are invited to the Sports Day held in the summer term.
From time to time other events, such as concerts and art exhibitions, take place at school and, in the hope they will be able to attend them, parents always receive information about these in plenty of time to make arrangements.
In the autumn and summer terms there are parents’ open evenings at which parents are able to visit all the classrooms in the school to observe the work on display throughout the school and to see their own child’s work.
We also hold ‘Family and Friends’ afternoons when lower school children are encouraged to bring their parents, grandparents or other members of their family to see round the school.
At the end of the summer term, two final assemblies are held, one in the Upper School (prize-giving) and one in the Lower School. Prizes are awarded to children in Year 6.
The Orchard House Parents’ Association (OHSPA)
The OHSPA is a great way to meet other parents and become better informed about issues and events affecting school life. The Association also aims to welcome and help new children and families to integrate into the school community.
All parents are automatically members. The Association does not deal with academic or curriculum aspects of the school or other matters within the prerogative of the headmaster.

The committee and form representatives normally meet twice each term. For the agendas of forthcoming meetings, parents with an item of interest or an activity to propose may contact either their form representative or the chairman.
The OHSPA may appoint sub-committees for special purposes (eg social activities such as the autumn’s social, the quiz night and the summer fair) and the OHSPA is keen to draw on the talents and energy of as many parents as possible in its activities.

Website and Parent Portal
As well as the information provided on this website, parents also have an account on the iSAMS parent portal which is a secure portal for parents. To access the portal, parents have a secure login, and all parents will be emailed when their child starts at the school with details on how to set up an account.
All circulars and copies of the Orchard Weekly are posted on the portal. At the beginning of every term an outline of the curriculum for each year group is also available on the portal.

Pastoral Care Comes First
Children blossom when they feel secure, happy, and valued. That’s why pastoral care sits at the heart of everything we do at Orchard House School. We place huge store on pastoral support in school to ensure every pupil gains the confidence to achieve their best, both academically and personally.
No child at Orchard House has any doubt that a teacher will lend a safe, sympathetic ear to their worries. Strong, trusting relationships between staff and pupils mean children feel genuinely supported – and confident children are children who thrive.
Relationships between staff and pupils are supportive and trusting, and consequently pupils are confident.
Building character, Nurturing Self
Some children have the good fortune to be privately educated at schools with the drive, experience, and resources to teach children to think critically and for themselves. At Orchard House School, children learn their personal choices can make a real difference, and their opinion matters.
Equally importantly, they learn to respect the opinions of others. They learn the value of endeavour and of staying power, of developing social skills, and of forming respectful relationships. Why do so many hands fly into the air when a teacher asks a question at Orchard House School? Our children feel confident and valued, so they are not worried about making mistakes and are willing to ‘have a go’.
This eagerness to be involved and to make a contribution is one of the most valuable life skills we nurture in our pupils.
The House System: Belonging and Teamwork
Orchard House’s six school Houses were chosen by our own pupils. Year 5 researched and presented on inspirational individuals whose values, actions, and achievements they felt reflected the spirit of our school. From these presentations, a shortlist was created and shared with the whole school, and every pupil then voted for the House name they felt best represented their community.
The result is a genuine, whole-school vote that gives pupils real ownership and pride in the House system:
Florence Nightingale
Children earn house points throughout the term, with house captains updating them of the scores weekly during assembly. The winning house is then presented with the house cup at the end of each term by Mrs Adams. House events include football, netball, the Petter Cup (music), and Sports Day.
Independent Thinking, Confidently Expressed
At a school with the drive, experience, and resources to teach children to think critically and for themselves, pupils learn that their personal choices can make a real difference – and that their opinion matters. Just as importantly, they learn to respect the opinions of others.
Through this, children develop the value of endeavour and staying power, alongside social skills and respectful relationships – the building blocks of confident, considerate young people.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is pastoral care in school?
Pastoral care in school refers to the support a school provides for a pupil’s emotional, social, and personal wellbeing, alongside their academic education. At Orchard House, this includes wellbeing questionnaires, individual Pupil Pastoral Plans, buddy and mentoring systems, and close, trusting relationships between staff and pupils.
How does Orchard House School support pupil wellbeing?
Every pupil completes a termly wellbeing questionnaire, which feeds into a personal Pupil Pastoral Plan. This allows teachers to monitor each child’s happiness and address any private worries proactively, rather than waiting for issues to escalate.
How does the House system support pastoral care?
Our six school Houses – Parks, Churchill, Nightingale, Mandela, Darwin, and Franklin – build teamwork, belonging, and healthy competition. Because pupils chose the House names themselves through a whole-school vote, the system gives children a genuine sense of ownership and community.
Why is pastoral care important in schools?
Children who feel secure, happy, and valued are more confident, more willing to take risks in their learning, and better equipped to develop strong social skills and respectful relationships – all of which support long-term academic and personal success.

The Learning Orchard Curriculum
A curriculum designed to prepare every child for the future.
The Learning Orchard has been developed to work alongside our exceptional teaching, to ensure our students are able to continue onto some of the best day and boarding schools in the UK.
Rooted within four guiding principles – Holistic Learning, Leadership, Powerful Knowledge, and World Readiness – the curriculum is designed to help children adapt to any terrain, preparing them not only for exams, but for all that comes next.
Teaching inspires pupils to care about real-world issues.
Download a Copy of The Learning Orchard
Inspiring a love of readingReading Explorer & Scholar Programmes
Our Reading Explorer and Reading Scholar programmes, designed for Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 respectively, reflect Orchard House School’s view that reading sits at the centre of children’s academic progress and supports their wellbeing. Regular time with books builds confidence, calm focus, vocabulary and comprehension. It also strengthens writing because pupils meet rich language and clear sentence patterns.
National data shows a sharp decline in children reading for pleasure, so we want to counter this trend. These programmes introduce pupils to high quality children’s literature, support positive reading habits and help children develop a genuine enjoyment of books.
How does it work?
Before each holiday the children receive a list of books to choose from, offering a range of difficulty levels including modern titles, classics, chapter books and picture books of high literary quality.
Pupils select a book to read during the break, or across the term if they need more time. They can read independently, have an adult read it to them or enjoy shared reading. This flexibility supports the programme’s purpose: to give children access to good literature and help them build a positive relationship with books.
When a child finishes a book they complete an explorer’s task linked to the text and after showing their completed activity to their class teacher, they receive a book exploration point. Ten points earn a Reading Explorer badge.
Pupils are challenged to read for at least 20 minutes each day, record the pages in their diary and complete a reflective sentence or two. Pupils are awarded 1-3 points for each book completed, depending on literary complexity, richness of vocabulary and the depth of its themes.
Pupils then complete an exit ticket for every book completed with 30 points earning a prestigious Reading Scholar badge, presented by our Head of School.
Since launching this year, the Reading Scholar programme has been so successful that we are now extending the initiative to include the Reading Critic, Ambassador and Laureate awards.
An ambitious and cohesive curriculum that focuses on pupils acquiring and applying new knowledge to real-world situations.

The Orchard House School Bursary Programme offers life-changing opportunities to bright, promising children whose families could not otherwise afford an independent fee-paying school.
Bursaries are awarded and funded by Orchard House School Educational Trust (OHSET), a registered charity which works closely with, but independently of, Orchard House School. OHSET raises funds year-round from the school community and supporters to make these opportunities possible.
Bursary applications for September 2027 are now open.

If you would like to register your interest in a bursary for September 2028 or beyond , please complete our interest form.

Year 3 (age 7); Years 4 or 5 occasionally considered

Application deadline
31 January for September entry that year; you can register your interest for future years at any time

How Our Bursaries Work
Your child may be eligible for a bursary if you can demonstrate the need for financial support.
You can register your interest for a future bursary place here.
Application timeline
Financial requirements
We do not set fixed income thresholds for bursary eligibility. Instead, we work with a specialist company to gain a clear and fair understanding of each family’s financial situation.
Our focus is on awarding transformational bursaries – typically covering 100% of fees – to children who would not otherwise be able to access private education.
As a general guideline, if your combined gross household income exceeds £100,000, it is unlikely that you would qualify for a bursary.
You can read the OHSET Privacy Policy here.
Frequently Asked Questions
What are the eligibility requirements for a bursary?
We look at both the child and family circumstances. We consider financial need, the likelihood that the child will thrive academically and socially at Orchard House, and how well the school can support the child’s development.
What is the typical entry point for bursary students
Most bursary awards are made for Year 3 entry, when children are 7 years old. Occasionally, bursaries may be available for entry into Years 4 or 5, depending on available funding and school places.
How do you check applicants' financial circumstances?
We partner with an independent financial assessment company that conducts a confidential, professional review of your family’s finances. This includes reviewing documents such as payslips, bank statements and tax returns, and may involve a home visit. The process ensures fairness and consistency for all applicants.
Is there a limit for my household income to be eligible for a bursary?
We don’t set strict income limits, but as a guide, families with a combined household income above £100,000 are unlikely to qualify. Each case is assessed individually by an independent specialist who considers the full financial picture, including income, assets and dependants.
What does a bursary cover?
Depending on your financial circumstances, a bursary may cover up to 100% of tuition fees. We may also assist with the cost of uniforms, educational trips and other essential items to ensure every child can participate fully in school life.
When can I apply for a bursary?
Applications for September 2026 entry opened in autumn 2025 and had to be submitted by 31 January 2026. You are welcome to register your interest for later years at any time using the interest form.
How many bursary places are available?
Typically, one or two new bursary places are awarded each year, depending on the availability of funds and suitable candidates.
Does Orchard House offer scholarships?
No. Orchard House School does not offer scholarships based on academic, musical or sporting achievement.
What's the difference between a scholarship and a bursary?
A scholarship is usually awarded for outstanding ability or talent in a particular area. A bursary is awarded based on financial need to ensure that a child who will thrive at Orchard House has the opportunity to do so regardless of family income.
What is your sibling policy for bursaries?
You are welcome to apply for a bursary for a sibling, but we cannot guarantee that bursaries will be available for multiple children in the same family. Each application is considered on its individual merits and subject to available funds.
Are children assessed based on their abilities?
Orchard House School is non-selective. Children take part in a relaxed, friendly assessment to help us understand their learning style and ensure they are happy and thrive in the school environment.

When you’re surrounded by leafy streets, period architecture and independent shops, it can be difficult to believe you’re still in London.
Yet that is precisely why families have been drawn here year-by-year, and why Orchard House School remains Chiswick’s premier prep school. Founded by the sons of Sylvia Rentoul (founder of our sister school Basset House in North Kensington), Orchard House School is a co-educational independent prep school for ages 3 to 11 in Chiswick. Nestled as we are between Bedford Park, Chiswick High Street and the Thames, we’ve been delivering quality education to West London as a prep school since 1993.
Since our acquisition by Dukes Education in 2020, we have merged with Chiswick & Bedford Park Preparatory School (CBPPS) to expand our reach and curriculum to more children. Now split across four sites, our bespoke Learning Orchard curriculum prepares children for the future while supporting them to be their best and growing their potential.
Whether you’re joining our Nursery or Early Years at Rupert Road, Pre-Prep at Priory Avenue or Prep at Newton Grove, Orchard House School is here to help every child flourish academically and personally.
Our Sites

Why Families Choose Orchard House School
Families looking for an independent prep school in Chiswick and West London want more than excellent academic results. They want a school where children are known as individuals, encouraged to develop confidence and curiosity and prepared for success both inside and outside the classroom.
At Orchard House School, we design every aspect of school life to help pupils flourish from Nursery through to Year 6.
Excellence
Learning at Orchard House is built around the school’s distinctive Learning Orchard curriculum and the internationally recognised High-Performance Learning framework, which encourages children to think independently, ask questions and develop a genuine love of learning.
Alongside core subjects, such as English, Mathematics and Science, we take great care to instil a love of philosophy and oracy in our pupils through regular Knowledge, Reasoning and Oracy lessons.
Creativity isn’t ignored here either, as Orchard House School encourages pupils to express themselves through the Arts and then apply those creative skills to STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts & Maths) projects.
Honesty
Every child learns differently, which is why Orchard House never hides anything from either its pupils or parents. From fees, admissions process and even your child’s progress – we believe in genuine, respectful relationships built on trust.
Combined with small class sizes and a personalised approach to teaching, teachers know each pupil very well, enabling them to celebrate strengths, nurture confidence and provide the right level of challenge as they progress.
Kindness
As a fully co-educational, non-selective independent prep school, Orchard House welcomes children from a wide range of backgrounds and abilities. Our pastoral care creates strong partnerships between staff, pupils and families, building an inclusive community where kindness, honesty and respect underpin everyday school life.
By leading with kindness, our children develop the ability to uplift those around them and create positive change in the world.
Academic Excellence & Outcomes
At Orchard House School, academic success is built on a broad and ambitious curriculum that encourages every child to become a confident, independent learner. Through the school’s distinctive Learning Orchard curriculum, alongside supplementary clubs and activities, pupils develop strong foundations across core subjects while benefiting from specialist teaching in music, sport, computing, drama and French. From Nursery onwards, subjects including science and art are taught separately, allowing children to deepen their knowledge and discover new interests.
Learning extends well beyond the classroom through the Orchard House Challenge, an enriched programme for Years 4 to 6 covering outdoor adventure, financial education, community service, the arts and personal development. Alongside initiatives such as the Reading Scholar and Explorer programmes, philosophy and oracy lessons, pupils are encouraged to become curious thinkers and confident communicators.
This commitment to educational excellence shows in our most recent ISI report, which states “The school’s work is regularly and thoroughly evaluated. Priorities for development are clearly identified and acted upon.”

Is Orchard House School a private school?
Yes. Orchard House School is an independent, fee-paying, non-selective prep school, inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) and a member of the Independent Association of Prep Schools (IAPS) and the Independent Schools Council (ISC).

Orchard House is fully co-educated from Nursery through Year 6, with small classes, a distinctive Learning Orchard curriculum and a strong record of scholarship success and offers from West London’s most competitive senior schools.
Which senior schools do Orchard House pupils go on to?
Recent leavers have secured places at schools including Latymer Upper School, Godolphin & Latymer School, Kew House School, Hampton School, Lady Eleanor Holles School and Ibstock Place School.
How do I apply to Orchard House School?

It’s never easy saying goodbye to your little ones on their first day of nursery.
At Orchard House School, our newly built nursery in Chiswick follows the same learning frameworks as the rest of the school, adapted for smaller children. When you entrust your children to us, you can expect physical, intellectual, emotional and social development in a safe, happy setting.

Our Approach to Early Learning
At Orchard House, our unique Learning Orchard curriculum helps your child reach their academic potential, but we go well beyond that. Children also benefit from many aspects of the Montessori curriculum and philosophy. Our spacious, innovative Early Years centre provides a safe, dynamic home for our Nursery and Reception classes, with generous classrooms, access to the Pre-Prep library at Priory House just down the road, and on-site outdoor play areas.

Settling In & the Move to Reception
We understand that starting nursery is a big step for children and parents alike, so we build settling in into our process from the outset. Before the summer term, our Head of EYFS and Head of Nursery contact each child’s previous nursery to discuss their transition. These assessments, known as EYFS profiles, are built from our accumulated observations and in-depth knowledge of your child, and parents are invited to contribute too. Because Nursery is our main entry point, offers come with a guaranteed pathway into Reception the following September. Parents can also choose to defer a Nursery offer to Reception entry, subject to availability, and children joining Reception are invited to a moving up day at the end of the summer term to prepare for September. Our admissions team give priority to siblings of current pupils and to children joining us from other Dukes Education nurseries.
Fees
We charge our fees so your child can have the best preparatory experience possible and receive a truly personal education. With your generosity, we have been able to provide better facilities and opportunities for our pupils, such as the new Early Years Rupert Road location.
As such, we believe in transparency so you can know exactly how much you will have to pay for your child to attend. Before we go through the Nursery fees, please know there is a non-refundable £100 registration fee, plus a £3000 acceptance deposit that is payable upon your child’s approved admission. Frequently Asked Questions
What age can my child start at Orchard House Nursery?
Children join Orchard House Nursery, in Chiswick, the September after they turn three. This is the school’s main entry point, with pupils automatically progressing into Reception the following academic year, subject to the standard admissions process.
Where is Orchard House Nursery located?
Orchard House Nursery is based at 2 Rupert Road, Chiswick, London, W4 – the school’s dedicated Early Years site, which also houses Reception. Children arrive at the side gate on Rupert Road, with staff and CCTV present at all arrival and departure times.
How many sessions per week can I book at Nursery?
We welcome Nursery pupils for a minimum of 5 sessions per week, with the option to choose mornings or afternoons. Additional sessions, up to 10 per week, can be added, and occasional one-off sessions are also available.
How much does Orchard House Nursery cost?
Nursery fees start from £4,123 per term for 5 sessions a week and rise according to the number of sessions booked, up to £8,234 for 10 sessions. Nursery fees are VAT-exempt and include a hot home-made lunch and most excursions.
Does Orchard House Nursery accept government-funded childcare hours?
Yes. We accept the 15-hour free childcare entitlement for eligible 3- to 4-year-olds, which is deducted from your termly invoice, and manage the application on your behalf. Working parents may also be eligible for an additional 30-hour funding allowance.
Will my child automatically progress from Nursery into Reception?
Nursery offers include a guaranteed pathway into Reception. Parents can also choose to defer a Nursery offer to Reception entry, subject to availability, as Reception places are extremely limited each year.
What curriculum does Orchard House Nursery follow?
Nursery follows the statutory Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework, delivered through Orchard House’s own Learning Orchard curriculum and Montessori-inspired provision, alongside specialist lessons in music, French, computing and PE.
Is Orchard House Nursery inspected by Ofsted or ISI?

Can I visit Orchard House Nursery before applying?
Yes. During term time we offer small group tours every Tuesday and Thursday morning at 10 am (booking required), along with private visits by appointment and two Open Mornings a year. We recommend visiting during term time to see the Nursery in full action.
How do I register my child for a Nursery place?

Our History The History of Orchard House School
The history of Orchard House School begins with our sister school, Bassett House in North Kensington, founded in 1947 by Sylvia Rentoul with just six pupils. At a time when education was often rigid and traditional, shaped by the belief that “children should be seen and not heard,” Sylvia introduced a philosophy that was ahead of its time. She believed passionately that children should be encouraged to express themselves, that learning should be both supportive and challenging, and that teaching must always take account of the unique needs of every child.
In 1993, inspired by Sylvia’s vision, her sons founded Orchard House School on its Newton Grove site. The school grew steadily, and in 2010 was expanded with the purpose-built Early Years building on Rupert Road. Sylvia’s child-centred approach not only endures but flourishes at Orchard House, forming the foundation of our ethos to this day.
In February 2020, Orchard House, together with Bassett House and Prospect House, joined Dukes Education. This marked a new chapter in the school’s story, opening up fresh opportunities for collaboration, innovation and growth.
Shortly afterwards, in 2021, Dukes Education acquired Chiswick & Bedford Park Preparatory School (CBPPS), a wonderful school just around the corner from Orchard House, with whom we shared much in common. Both schools had long histories of academic excellence and strong moral ethos, and a deep commitment to nurturing each child as an individual. Over the following two years, Orchard House and CBPPS worked closely together under the joint leadership of Kit Thompson (then Head of Orchard House) and Henrietta Adams (then Head of CBPPS), ensuring a positive and enriching experience for pupils at both schools.
Today, under the leadership of Head Henrietta Adams, Orchard House is a fully merged and united community. Our pupils wear a new uniform that reflects our shared identity, and they are taught by a dedicated, talented team who are committed to providing the very best education. We are proud that our most recent Year 6 cohort received 150 senior school offers and over 40 scholarships across music, art, drama, sport, chess and academics.
Our innovative curriculum, The Learning Orchard, has already been shortlisted for the TES Primary Curriculum Leader of the Year Award, and, alongside our outstanding pastoral care, ensures children flourish not only academically, but also in confidence, creativity, and kindness.
From Sylvia Rentoul’s pioneering ideals to the thriving school we are today, Orchard House has always placed children at the centre of everything we do. Her vision of education, joyful, individualised, and forward-looking, continues to shape our future and remains at the heart of our community.
Our HistoryA Leading Light
In 2023, the nurseries of Orchard House and Chiswick & Bedford Park Preparatory School came together, and by September 2024 the two schools had fully merged under the Orchard House name. This marked the beginning of an exciting new chapter in our history, blending the strengths and traditions of both schools into a single, united community.
As part of the merger, our main school buildings underwent a full refurbishment: Rupert Road now houses our Early Years, Priory Avenue our Key Stage 1 pupils, and Newton Grove our Key Stage 2. Alongside this cosmetic transformation, we have invested in new specialist teaching spaces, including a state-of-the-art Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Maths (STEAM) Centre, enhanced facilities for Music and Drama, and a broader timetable of enrichment activities and clubs. This seven-figure investment from Dukes Education firmly establishes Orchard House as one of London’s premier preparatory schools.
Today, as a thriving three-form entry school, every child benefits from the support of a full-time teaching assistant as well as specialist teaching staff across the curriculum. This ensures that academic excellence is delivered hand-in-hand with exceptional pastoral care.
While we look confidently to the future, we also continue to honour the proud heritage of Chiswick & Bedford Park School, working closely with our community to celebrate its legacy as part of our shared story.

Orchard House School is a co-educational Pre-Prep and Prep School in London, welcoming children from Year 1 through to Year 6. Every teacher shares one firm belief: nurturing individuality is the most effective way of teaching children to fly. With a high ratio of staff to pupils, highly qualified teachers and a dedicated team of teaching assistants, we ensure every child receives the personal attention they need to thrive.
Intellectual curiosity and in-depth learning are encouraged through research, general knowledge homework, open-ended investigations and collaborative learning activities – all delivered through The Learning Orchard curriculum, our rich, stimulating and challenging approach to education that helps pupils develop their skills and passions from their very first day with us to their last.

Understanding Our Pre-Prep and Prep Structure
Orchard house is set-up intentionally to provide children with support at every stage of their academic journey. With clear goals and pathways from early years up until their transition to senior school.
Foundations of confidence, curiosity and independence
Building strong academic foundations through inspiring, hands-on learning

Each stage builds deliberately on the one before it, so children progress with confidence rather than experiencing sudden change. Pupils are taught by the same close-knit community of staff throughout their Orchard House journey, meaning strong relationships — and a genuine understanding of each child as an individual — are carried through from Pre-Prep into Prep and beyond.
Pre-Prep: Years 1 & 2 (Ages 5–7)
In Pre-Prep, children build on the strong start they’ve had in Early Years, growing in confidence, independence and curiosity. Lessons are designed to nurture a love of learning through rich stories, hands-on exploration and specialist teaching in subjects including Art, Music, PE, French and Drama, alongside core skills in English, Maths and Science.
Pupils benefit from small class sizes and a high staff-to-pupil ratio, ensuring the personal attention every child needs to build a genuinely strong foundation before moving into Prep.
Prep: Years 3–6 (Ages 7–11)
As pupils move into Prep, they enter a more ambitious, academically focused stage of learning. Our bespoke Learning Orchard curriculum blends Powerful Knowledge, Holistic Learning, Leadership and World Readiness, encouraging pupils to think deeply, question confidently and develop a genuine love of learning.
STEAM projects link Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Maths; coding is introduced from Year 1 onwards in our dedicated Innovation Hub; and termly assessments in English, Maths, Science and Reasoning feed into individual target setting, so every pupil is stretched and supported appropriately as they work towards senior school entry.
STEAM Learning
STEAM lessons for pupils in Prep involve projects that link Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Maths. Computing lessons include coding skills from Year 1 upwards in our dedicated Innovation Hub.
English lessons incorporate engaging and imaginative novels, poetry and non-fiction texts to develop pupils’ reading and writing skills and inspire a life-long love of reading, supported by weekly library lessons in our extensively stocked libraries.
Termly assessments in English, Maths, Science and Reasoning from Year 1 upwards feed into target setting, enabling staff to tailor the curriculum to individual pupils, enhance progress and ensure every child is appropriately challenged. Assessment results and targets are shared with parents throughout the year.
Performing Arts
Our school is equipped with specialist teaching facilities for Science & Computing, Art, Design Technology and Music alongside dedicated multi-purpose halls and rooms used for assemblies, Drama and performance. Musical and Performing Arts play a key role at Orchard House School, with pupils of all ages participating in drama and musical productions, clubs, concerts and assemblies. Musical performance groups include Orchestra, String Group and School Choir.

Why Families Choose Orchard House for Pre-Prep and Prep School in London
What is the difference between a Pre-Prep and a Prep School?
Pre-Prep typically covers the early primary years (Reception to Year 2), focusing on building strong academic and social foundations. Prep School continues from Year 3 to Year 6, moving into a more ambitious, subject-specialist stage of learning that prepares pupils for senior school entry, including the 11+. At Orchard House, both stages sit within one continuous school, so children move between them without changing site, community or ethos.
What age does Pre-Prep start at Orchard House?
Pre-Prep at Orchard House covers Years 1 and 2, for children aged 5 to 7. Children join us even earlier, from age 3, through our Early Years provision at Nursery and Reception.
What age does Prep School finish, and what comes next?
Prep School at Orchard House covers Years 3 to 6, for children aged 7 to 11. In Year 6, pupils move on to senior school, supported by our dedicated Senior Schools & 11+ programme, which combines exam coaching with interview preparation.
Is Orchard House a co-educational Prep School?
Yes. Orchard House is a co-educational Pre-Prep and Prep School, welcoming both boys and girls throughout Pre-Prep and Prep.
Do pupils need to sit an entrance exam to join Pre-Prep or Prep?
Entry requirements vary by year group and point of entry. Our Admissions team can talk you through the process for your child’s specific age group, and details for international families are also available on our Welcoming International Families page.
What support is available for children who need extra help?
Our dedicated Learning Support team works with pupils across Pre-Prep and Prep, identifying needs early and tailoring support so every child can access the curriculum with confidence.
How can I find out more or arrange a visit?
We’d love to show you around. You can book a private tour or apply for a place directly through our website or contact our Admissions team at info@orchardhs.org.uk or 020 8742 8544.

The school meets all the required Standards set out in the Education (Independent School Standards) Regulations 2014, including those relating to leadership and management, the quality of education, safeguarding, pupils’ physical and mental health, and their social and economic education.
